verdict.rationale: Independent community reports describe strong backwards compatibility and superior documentation. Babylon.js also serves llms.txt files and offers an interactive Playground for sharing code, and probe data shows 234,040 weekly npm downloads for @babylonjs/core. However, nothing directly shows LLM-generated code working on the first try, and one commenter notes three.js is better known, which suggests fewer public examples. Docs are client-rendered with no .md mirrors. Missing for 10: hands-on evidence of LLM first-try success, evidence that public example volume is abundant, machine-readable markdown docs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, LLM-generated code mostly works on the first try — stable, well-documented APIs with abundant public examples the models have seen

citations.quote: the documentation and backwards compatibility is quite something
ThreeJS's API breaks backwards compatibility a lot, while Babylon is exactly the opposite. Babylon also has vastly superior documentation
BOTH doc.babylonjs.com and www.babylonjs.com serve llms.txt files
